To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a series of polymeric materials, including chitosan, PEA, PHEA, and a series of copolymers of ethyl acrylates, hydroxyethyl, and methyl acrilates, can be used to support the attachment and differentiation of neural stem cell cultures.
poly(ethyl acarylate)-based copolymer surfaces promote the differentiation of neural cells into functional neurons and astrocytes.
a series of polymeric copolymers, including ethyl acrylates and hydroxyethyl acylates, can promote differentiation of postnatal NSCs into functional cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biomaterials with a defined surface chemistry that are suitable for the culture of NSCs and that promote their differentiation into functional neurons and astrocytes.

the differentiation of postnatal NSCs and with the development of new polymeric biomaterial substrates that could be used to study NSCs in vitro and to promote their differentiation into functional neurons.
the development of new biomaterials for tissue engineering applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the copolymers PEA and PEA/PHEA are the most promising substrates for neuronal differentiation and functional maturation.
PEA/PHEA copolymers are suitable substrates for promoting the differentiation of adult NSC into functional neurons and that the composition of the copolymers influences the extent of differentiation.
PEA-based copolymers are the most effective substrates to support NSC attachment and differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the copolymer PEA/HHEA 50/50 is the best substrate for the differentiation of adult NSC into functional neurons.

a combination of poly(ethyl acylate) and poly(hydroxy ethyl acylate) in a narrow composition ratio is the optimal substrate for differentiation of NSCs into neurons, whereas a combination of poly(hydroxy acylate) with either poly(ethyl acrlate) or poly(methyl acylate), or both, is the optimal substrate to promote the differentiation into glia.
the copolymers of PEA/PHEA in a composition window of 20/80 and 30/70 are good candidates for the culture of NSCs and the differentiation of these cells into functional neurons and astrocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composition of the copolymer is critical for promoting cell attachment, neuronal differentiation, and the formation of functional synapses.
a combination of polymeric biomolecules with specific chemical and physical properties can be used for the differentiation of NSCs into functional neuronal networks.
a series of poly(alkyl acrylate) copolymers can be employed for the differentiation of adult NSC into neurons and glia.
